title: Choose the visual world for CloudOps Intelligence
question: The roll assigned Review Bench (code-review diff view). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Review Bench
options.lineage: GitHub / Gerrit code review — split diff, gutter markers, review comments, status checks
options.thesis: An answer is a change request: claims on the left, the evidence that justifies each on the right, and a checks line that says whether it may merge into your incident.
options.viewport: A top command bar (query field, role chip, strategy chip). Below, a two-pane bench: LEFT the answer as numbered claim lines with gutter markers [S1]…; RIGHT the cited section as a line-numbered evidence file with the supporting lines highlighted; between them hairline connectors from marker to lines. A CHECKS strip under the answer: Retrieval 42→38→20→6 · Citations 5/5 valid · Evidence strength HIGH · Conflicts 1 (as a review comment pinned to the claim it affects). Incidents and Explorer live as tabs in the bar, not a sidebar.
options.risk: If the evidence pane is not genuinely line-addressable, it collapses into two columns of cards and the metaphor reads as decoration.

raised.raise: Ranked rows never reflow: the retrieval trail and incident list are column-locked tables whose rows change state in place (delayed → amber, withheld → dim red), never re-laid out.
One ink, one ramp: evidence strength and rerank scores render as a single-hue luminance ramp on the accent, not a traffic light.
Fixed-scale plates: every source card shares one exact scale and baseline so five sources compare at a glance; nothing grows because it ranked first.
Packet → sheet: the retrieval trail rests as a one-line packet under the answer and deploys in one pull into the full stage sheet, then folds back; no accordion of accordions.
Selection floods the readout: choosing a citation floods the evidence pane header and gutter with that source's tint so you always know which file you are reading.

regions.label: evidence file · line numbers · highlighted lines

options.label: Console Panes
options.lineage: k9s / htop / tmux — a TUI incident console
options.thesis: The knowledge base as one more pane in the on-call engineer's terminal: everything keyboard-driven, everything monospace, status bar at the bottom.
materials: bottom status bar with key hints
options.viewport: Three tiled panes: query + answer (left, tall), sources (right top), trail/status (right bottom); a status bar shows role, strategy, latency, cost and the key bindings.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for a developer-facing AI tool; many terminal-styled assistants exist, so it reads as expected rather than as this product.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Every retrieval stage, source and incident is a ranked row on a board whose columns never move; state changes flip in place.
options.viewport: A full-width board: rows are sources ranked by fused score, columns SID · title · section · version · score · state; the answer sits above as the board's headline line.
options.case: Fuses well for lists (trail, incidents, sources) and holds product clarity there; loses audience identification — engineers don't read their tools as a concourse — and prose answers have no row to live in.
options.risk: Per-character flip motion becomes noise on every update unless reserved for genuine state changes.

options.label: Phosphor Glyph Grid
options.case: Novelty outranks clarity: an operator cannot read a runbook through a luminance ramp of glyphs.
options.kept: One ink, one ramp — a single-hue luminance scale for scores instead of a traffic light.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: Cream paper and engraved italics are the opposite of an incident console's physical scene (dark room, many tabs, 2 a.m.); loses both axes.
options.kept: Fixed-scale plates on one baseline — sources compare because nothing changes size by rank.

options.label: Racing League Livery
options.case: Speed livery contradicts the product's promise of calm, verifiable evidence; loses both axes.
options.kept: Selection floods the readout — the chosen citation tints the evidence pane so the active file is unmistakable.

options.label: Miura Fold
options.case: White paper and gold foil are a persuasion material, not an operator's; the crease grid fights tabular data. Loses both axes.
options.kept: Packet → sheet deployment — the trail collapses to one line and opens in a single motion.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.case: Type-as-weather cannot carry a citation, a role, or a table; loses both axes and offers no discipline this product lacks.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Sidebar of past queries, centered search, answer with numbered footnotes, source cards below — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar; centered query field; answer card; row of source cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Perplexity/Glean-style tools by design — the arrangement the project specification explicitly warns against.
